We have a retrosynthetic template that suggests disconnection into two precursors: COc1ccc(Br)cc1 (bromo anisole) and COc1ccc(C(C)=O)cc1 (p-anisaldehyde? Actually anisaldehyde with methyl ketone? Wait: COc1ccc(C(C)=O)cc1 is anisyl methyl ketone (p-methoxyacetophenone). The product is the target: a stilbene with two anisole rings (para-methoxy phenyl) attached via C=C double bond. The template suggests a Heck coupling between aryl bromide and aryl ketone? Actually the product is a stilbene with two anisole rings, each para-methoxy. The precursors: bromo anisole (para? Actually COc1ccc(Br)cc1 is anisole with bromine at para? The SMILES: COc1ccc(Br)cc1 is anisole with bromine at para? The ring: COc1ccc(Br)cc1: methoxy at position 1, bromine at position 4 (para). The other: COc1ccc(C(C)=O)cc1 is anisole with acetyl group (COCH3) at para. So the reaction is a Heck coupling of aryl bromide with aryl ketone? Actually Heck typically couples aryl halide with alkene. Here the product is a double bond between the aryl carbon bearing carbonyl and the aryl carbon bearing bromine? Wait product is C=C between the two aryl rings, each para-methoxy. The template suggests forming the double bond via a Wittig? But the template shows Br-aryl + aryl ketone -> stilbene? The retro template: product -> Br-aryl + aryl ketone. So forward reaction: Br-aryl + aryl ketone -> product via maybe a cross-coupling (Knoevenagel condensation? Actually aryl ketone (acetophenone) can undergo aldol condensation with aldehyde? Not. Could be a McMurry coupling of two carbonyls? But we have only one carbonyl. Hmm.

Nevertheless, we have precursors that are commercially available: p-bromo anisole (4-bromoanisole) and p-anisyl methyl ketone (4-methoxyacetophenone). Need to check buyability and price constraints (<$150 total). Use is_buyable for both.
